For the first problem, we have been talking to LG's friend's store for three weeks and they tell us that they do not replace the product because we did not report it on the delivery note (thank goodness we reported it when we received the product) and they did not return the money because three weeks have passed (which have passed because they have not answered emails at any time, while I have called day after day during these three weeks. I find it outrageous that a company like LG, to which you report damage to the product when you receive a product, waits for the warranty period to expire so they don't replace the product or refund your money. I would really think about going back to buying a product directly from a company that bets on playing with the times despite its own mistakes

Sentence (English): The product arrived on April 18th at around 6pm, and an hour later we reported a defect/peeling in the corner to the LG friend's store.
Comments (English): [ Terrible product and customer service ] || ---------------- || The product arrived on April 18th at around 6pm, and an hour later we reported a defect/peeling in the corner to the LG friend's store. The first wash was OK, from then on every time we used the dishwasher we got a BE error (excess amount of detergent). For the first problem we have been talking to LG's friend's store for three weeks and they tell us that they will not replace the product because we did not report it on the delivery note (thank goodness we reported it when we received the product) and they will not give us our money back because three weeks have passed (which have passed because they have not answered the emails at any time, while I have called day after day during these three weeks. We reported the problem of excess dishwasher directly to LG on May 5, tired of not receiving a response from LG's friend's store and after having to dry the dishes by hand and having to suffer 6-hour wash cycles to remove the error, with the consequent water and electricity consumption. I find it outrageous that a company like LG, to which you report when you receive a product with nicks on the product, deliberately waits for the warranty period to pass in order not to replace the product or give you your money back. I would think very hard about buying a product directly from a company that gambles with timing. despite his own mistakes
Comments (Original): [ Producto y atencion al cliente nefasta ] || ---------------- || llegó el producto el día 18 de abril sobre las 18 de la tarde, y reportamos una hora despues un desperfecto/descascarillado en la esquina a la tienda del amigo de LG. Para el primer problema llevamos tres semanas hablando con la tienda del amigo de LG y nos dicen que no nos reponen el producto porque no lo reportamos en el albaran (menos mal que lo reportamos a la hora de recibir el producto) y no nos devuelven el dinero porque han pasado tres semanas (las cuales han pasado porque no han contestado en ningún momento a los correos, mientras yo he llamado día tras día durante estas tres semanas. El problema de exceso de lavavajillas lo reportamos directamente a LG el día 5 de mayo, cansados de no recibir respuesta por parte de la tienda del amigo de LG y despues de tener que secar nosotros a mano la vajilla y tener que sufrir ciclos de lavado de 6 horas para quitar el error, con el consumo de agua y luz consecuente. Me parece indignante que una empresa como LG a la que le reportas a la hora de recibir un producto picotazos en el producto, se esperen aposta a que pase el periodo de garantia para no reponerte el producto ni devolverte tu dinero. Me pensaría mucho volver a comprar un producto directamente en una empresa que aposta juega con los tiempos pese a sus propios errores

Here are the other things I can say about it:- The cycles are very, very long. The plastic parts that are meant to hold utensils are spaced together so closely, it's difficult to fit anything with a handle wider than 1/2”. It is also so shallow, it won't accommodate any dishes much taller than a regular shot glass.-The tines on the middle and bottom racks do not do a good job of holding the dishes. When the racks are pulled out, the dishes roll all around and need to be repositioned after pushing the rack back in. - THE DISHES DON'T GET CLEAN! - THE DISHES DON'T GET DRY! After the cycle is completed, I open the door to take the dishes out, and there's water dripping all over the dishes and the inside of the dishwasher. It's like the dishwasher decided to spray water all over the dishes after the drying cycle. I've had this dishwasher for two months, and every time I use it, I say, “I hate this dishwasher so much! ” My husband said we'll keep it a year and get a different one when we remodel our kitchen. I might end up washing dishes by hand and using this dishwasher as a drying rack for the next year!

A bonus oven rack jet-thingy that makes it possible to use the DW for that awkward job is something I look forward to using. We probably don't need the cutlery basket as well as the cutlery drawer, but it was a nod to the old M500 which we didn't realise we could do without. As this is our third large appliance from Bosch we are used to the ease of adjusting the programs to suit our requirements and couldn't be happier with each of the units plus the after-sales service. We probably won't see this DW out, but I think we have upgraded the look of our kitchen for when we sell the house in 3-4 years.

Sentence (English): I am loyal Bosch customer and until this purchase always recommended the dishwashers to my friends.
Comments (English): [ Sold a lemon ] || ---------------- || I am loyal Bosch customer and until this purchase always recommended the dishwashers to my friends. This dishwasher came from the factory with a bad heat pump which made a horrible smell when the dishwasher was run. While fixing this, the Bosch approved technician discovered there was an electrical problem as well and we were told not to have power to the unit for safety reasons. For a month, I have been trying to communicate with Bosch support to try to get a replacement for this unit that even Bosch support people say could not be sold because it would be considered a refurbished unit. To date, I still do not have a working product. I am extremely disappointed in the Bosch product and the treatment of the support department workers who did not do what they told me they would many times. I will never buy another Bosch product again and will share my experiences with others.

Sentence (English): My previous dishwasher was a Fagor that was more than 11 years old, so compared to that one, this one is quieter.
Comments (English): [ Wash well ] || ---------------- || My previous dishwasher was a Fagor that was more than 11 years old, so compared to that one, this one is quieter. I have to say that the distribution of the trays seems much worse to me in this dishwasher and the feeling is that there is room for considerably fewer things than in the old one, I especially don't like the top tray. I am using the eco program, which lasts 3 and a half hours and is supposed to be the one with the least consumption of all the programs. I will see on the next bill if this is noticeable and I will update the review. As a plus point, it washes well, in the approximately month that I've been using it I haven't had a bad wash (I put everything in, pans, pots.) Maybe I expected more for the price. It is exactly the same as another brand that my sister has and she paid much less. I hope it lasts at least as long as my last dishwasher.

Es exactamente igual al de otra marca que tiene mi hermana y pagó mucho menos ...espero que dure, por lo menos, como mi último lavavajillas.

I also have a really hard time starting my washing machine because the beep is so quiet and the start button in particular seems to be incredibly hard to sense my finger touch. On average, I have to hit the button about five times before it will finally start. I have tried hitting it very gently and slow, pressing hard, and all in between. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't and I just have to keep pressing until it finally starts.

Sentence (English): My daughter and I visited the Belmont store on a Thursday night after our original 9yr old LG dishwasher broke down.
Comments (English): [ Incorrect order and poor customer service ] || ---------------- || My daughter and I visited the Belmont store on a Thursday night after our original 9yr old LG dishwasher broke down. There were 2 LG dishwashers on sale at the same price. Upon waiting for someone to serve us and then having to go to the counter to find someone, I asked the salesman what the difference was. He explained the one at the front was the old model and the one in the aisle was the newer model and had 3 draws and was larger inside. I said we would take that one. Then upon trying to place the order on the computer, the system was down. I after a lengthy wait, it worked and I paid for the dishwasher. I also wanted to arrange delivery and install. Unfortunately that side of the system wasnt available, but the salesman named Marco said he would contact me the next day to arrange that. He called and we booked for the following Friday. He said the delivery company would contact me on the day. I waited at home all morning to be contacted and then received a message saying 11am. I waited and waited only then the notification was deleted. When I called, they informed me they werent able to deliver for a month. I was quite shocked and disappointed. I then arranged some family to take time off work to come down and pick it up. After they opened it all up and showed me, we realised we had been given the older LG model. Not the one we had requested. Unfortunately on the night as I mentioned the prices were the same and they were both LG. I assumed he had selected the correct one that we were standing over, when I said we would take it! Upon trying to correct this error, the staff were incredibly rude and not accommodating for their own error. This led us to then asking for a refund and we have since purchased the correct model from elsewhere and loving it! I will not be shopping again at the good guys Belmont

Comments (English): [ Not as good as GE profile model from 12 years ago. ] || ---------------- || Any review claiming this is a loud dishwasher may have had an installation problem like mine. The Costco hired installers said they did not have these parts and they were not even supposed to be part of this model (wrong, installation instructions even show them) and walked away leaving a really loud dishwasher (this was after having a previous 12 year old GE profile that was whisper quiet, but unfortunately broke down, so I knew better). After calling GE service, I eventually got the missing parts delivered for this model. GE service would not install them (said it was part of installers job), so I installed them myself, and the unit is now as quiet as my old model. Amazing what these sound dampers do for the noise. I will also say, this unit does not hold as many dishes as the old GE profile model, and the door seems a lot more flimsy, so a step backwards in quality and design. I was looking at the highly rated Bosch models, but there was too long a backlog for those deliveries. Next time I will wait. This will be my last GE. I have no problem buying an appliance from Costco and I'm sure their concierge service would have helped resolve the installation if I was willing to wait rather than do it myself.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher is much quieter than the 15 year old GE we recently replaced.
Comments (English): [ Good overall ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is much quieter than the 15 year old GE we recently replaced. The manual had good tips for hot to load and use the features for maximum cleaning and drying. There is a night time dry feature that removes the humid air when the cycle finishes if leaving it overnight so the dishes are drier. We still always have some moisture left, particularly on plastics. The three racks are nice, and the middle is adjustable up/down. Removed a star for the install, they dropped a tool on the dishwasher door that they had opened and the tool left a dent. It didn't impact the function at all, but just know that the inside stainless steel will dent easily. Also the installers did not center it in the opening well, leaving a slight gap to the side. I asked if they could center it but they said no. Just be sure to watch when they install, make sure it is level and centered- ours was not. Overall it was a very competitive price that included the delivery, install, and haul away of the old appliance so we are happy. Will update if the washer's performance changes, right now it cleans very well.

Sentence (English): Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews.
Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Sentence (English): Price range: up to 200,000 won.
Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Sentence (English): I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once.
Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Sentence (English): I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!
Comments (English): [ Since my kitchen is small and there are only two people, I looked for a small dishwasher for a while and ended up buying the Chefborn Washpole 4, which had the most reviews. I compared it with other brands (Coo* / Midi* / S* Magic) and bought it. ] || ---------------- || Since my kitchen is small and I live with two people, I searched for a compact dishwasher for quite some time before deciding on the Chefborn Washpoll 4, which had the most reviews. Here are a few things I focused on when comparing it to other brands (Coo*, Midi*, and S*Magic): 1. Price range: up to 200,000 won. 2. Suction-type, not tank-type. 3. A glass window to ensure it washes well. 4. A drying function after washing. 5. An automatic door-opening feature. 6. Installation-free operation. The Washpoll 4 met all of these criteria, so I chose it. I set an alarm and bought it during a live event, which made it a bit more affordable. Actually, I've been arguing a few times over dishwashing since I moved in with my partner, so I figured I'd just get a dishwasher instead. Ultimately, the time I spent thinking about it was well spent, and it's been working great ever since it arrived. That was the most important factor and my motivation for purchasing. There were no more arguments. So, I really didn't regret the price. The interior space. I think it's big enough to store all the dishes for two people at once. Sometimes, when the lunch box is empty, I have to run it twice, and I only wash the large frying pans by hand. It even fits small pots and pans. For a mini dishwasher, the interior seems quite large, so I'm very satisfied with it. Noise. I was worried because some people complained about the noise, but it wasn't a problem for us at all. It's the sound of the water running, so it's not overly annoying. However, I don't think it's appropriate to run it while sleeping in a studio apartment. There's also a hot air dryer noise after washing. If you have a separate kitchen or a 1.5-room apartment, the noise shouldn't be a big issue. The hot air dryer automatically turns on after the washing cycle (after about 90 minutes of washing mode), so you can hear the fan quietly. Washing, too. I did a pre-wash and then ran it, and everything was fine. I tried putting in hardened parts that weren't soaked in water for a test, and these were definitely harder to clean. If you soak only the hardened parts in water and put them in, I think it will be okay to clean them. And if you wash them with hot water, they come off cleanly without any oil, which is nice. As for the installation difficulty. Since you just have to connect the pipes, it wasn't difficult at all. However, if you want to organize the wires more neatly after installing the pipes, you'll probably need to buy a few cable management items from Daiso. Since I bought it to use it without installation, the installation difficulty was easy! Overall, it's one of the most satisfying purchases I've made recently. I recommend it to people living alone or in a two-person household who suffer from washing dishes~!

Comments (English): [ Works as a dishwasher should ] || ---------------- || I've lived in my house for just shy of 6 years and just bought a third dishwasher. They really only make them to last a max of 5yr now, sadly. Because we've had to purchase two in that time, we decided to buy a more simple/basic model this time. It's a tad louder than I'd like but it cleans fine. The timer is off - it'll say 2hr8min for an cycle and yet 2.5hr will go buy and it'll STILL running, but when finished it's clean and dry. Dries better than my old model. Only real issue we've had is exactly 30 days after installation the door hinge broke and it would drop hard and fast to the floor. Because it was under warranty, a licensed GE repair person was at my house the next business day to repair that for free. The insulation on the unit had gotten caught in the hinge stuff, so it was an easy fix. Just a weird fluke. Hoping this new model lasts at least the 5yr. I do like all of my GE appliances.

I've asked for a trade in, paying the difference, or a refund so I can get the highly rated Bosch. Customer service insists I get a repair guy to fix the defects. I do not find this satisfactory. I reiterated my concerns and request for resolution and have been ignored. I would NOT recommend the model I have and cannot verify if their new model is as good as claimed. I do know my old Asko was far better and I suspect the Bosch dishwasher is much better than my LG.

It's more like a chevy. Regardless of the detergent I use, water spots. While it has a sanitizing option, there is no heated dry option and we must take a dishtowel to dry them - EVERYTIME, before they can be put in the cabinets and drawers or they have to air dry overnight or for several hours. This just creates more and tougher water spots. It cleans okay, but we would never consider not rinsing them well prior to - especially if it is not a full load and it will be a day or two before we run it. Sentence (English): We bought two of these, and compared to our older, top-of-the-line, KitchenAid dishwashers three notables stand out.
Comments (English): [ A new learning experience. ] || ---------------- || We bought two of these, and compared to our older, top-of-the-line, KitchenAid dishwashers three notables stand out. 1. Because everything you load is more spaced out, everything comes out remarkably and sparkling clean.3. So we are very pleased :)Recommendation: Our spoons and forks do not fit in (without exaggeration) half of the allocated slots. This almost seems intentional and probably is (as it mimics the rack spacing for dishes to allow better cleaning between forks and spoons).

Sentence (English): A dishwasher I received as a surprise gift from my boyfriend.
Comments (English): [ I am extremely satisfied. ] || ---------------- || A dishwasher I received as a surprise gift from my boyfriend. It is by far the best appliance I’ve bought this year. But I was seriously surprised by how big and heavy the box was. I had no idea it would be this big. Thanks also to my boyfriend for lifting it onto the sink to install it. Installation was difficult at all; I just plugged it in and it was done in a snap. Actually, I worried a lot before and after buying it because people said it was noisy and didn't clean as well as expected. I was concerned if it would be okay since it wasn't cheap. My past self was something else... Finally, I am free from washing dishes. It is wider than I thought and holds a lot! Most importantly, it cleans well! I was worried about the drying part because I saw reviews saying it doesn't dry completely. It does dry a bit. Actually, it is damp. Oh! But if you leave the door wide open and take out all the baskets, the water evaporates quickly. + In two months, it will be exactly one year since I started using it. It has become a precious dishwasher that I can't live without now. It hasn't broken down a single time while I've been using it. To those complaining about detergent sticking everywhere because it didn't dissolve: if you break a detergent bottle into quarters, it won't leave marks! Sentence (English): This is an excellent LG Dishwasher, even though the huge 10 year warranty sticker on it is a Scam.
Comments (English): [ This is an excellent LG Dishwasher, 10 year warnty ] || ---------------- || This is an excellent LG Dishwasher, even though the huge 10 year warranty sticker on it is a Scam. Hands down better then the Whirlpool dishwasher I just replaced. - Pro's - Great looks and beautiful styling with a front panel to turn it on and off. I simply hate dishwashers with buttons on top of the door where you can't even monitor washing progress, this washer has an awesome front display countdown timer. - Full Stainless steel tub washing area, not plastic, not hybrid, but steel which means the dishwasher will never have a mildew rotting smell that the newer plastic dishwashers give. - Quad wash system does do a great job of washing dishes, more then a marketing gimic. - Really good dish drying system - LG has done an excellent job of designing the tub area which is really large and allows for huge loads of dishes Con's - LG continues to put huge eyesore hard to remove 10 year warranty stickers on all their dishwashers. This claim by LG is a scam and gives buyers a false sense of security about a 10 year warranty. I recently had my couple year old LG at my cottage die, turns out this 10 year LG dishwasher warranty only covers Inverter Direct Drive Motor Parts, not labour or replacement in anyway. The labour costs I was quoted was $550 for a technician to come to my place, diagnose, give me a document to send to LG for a replacement motor and for him to then come over and do a big install. This 10 year warranty sticker on all LG products is a scam. - LG actually reduced all dishwasher parts and labour warranty in May 2022 to only 1 year. Tub warranty was reduced from 5 years down to 2 years parts only. Considering LG themselves is restricting warranty, it doesn't exactly inspire customer confidence in this brand at all. They are literately trying to tell you this is a disposable dishwasher, when it dies, it dies, walk away, throw it away, they don't want to fix it either. - The dishwasher is moderately quiet, if you stand near it or in the kitchen you will hear it, but if you leave the kitchen it is almost silent. If you live in a house, this is a non issue, if you live in a studio apartment where your bed and soda are all near the dishwasher, maybe look for something more expensive and quieter. Conclusion: While this is an excellent dishwasher that I would have given 5 stars to, the glass is half full for me since LG's false promises with huge almost impossible to remove stickers that make customers think they have a 10 year warranty, when it's really only 1 and an extra year from Costco. LG has suckered me once with this sticker, I feel sorry for others who fall for it also.

Overall, I'm happy but I don't think the extra features are worth it so don't hesitate in getting the 300 series.

Sentence (English): The Bosch SMV8YCX03E dishwasher replaced the very old, 22-year-old Whirpool dishwasher - both from the top shelf.
Comments (English): [ New dishwasher - new life ] || ---------------- || The Bosch SMV8YCX03E dishwasher replaced the very old, 22-year-old Whirpool dishwasher - both from the top shelf. Are twenty years of development in dishwashing technology visible? After almost a month of use, I must say YES. The dishwasher is really quiet - you can hardly hear it, although of course you have to get used to the new sounds, especially the "purring" during drying. Sentence (English): Our old Bosch Dishwasher lasted 13 or 14 years.
Comments (English): [ Replaced Old Bosch with New Bosch ] || ---------------- || Our old Bosch Dishwasher lasted 13 or 14 years. Extremely happy with the original dishwasher. However, we did have to replace the lower basket 3 years ago as the rubber coating broke through and the underlying metal was rusting and causing some cleaning issues. Replacing the basket was a little pricy for a metal basket covered with rubber. But we bought on the 2ndary market. I hope the new dishwasher lasts at least as long. But on-to the reason for the reduced star. Pros: We thought the old dishwashwer was already quiet. This one is quieter than the old Bosch. We thought about the new Bosh that's even quieter than this one for double this price, but are quite happy we didn't. This dishwasher is quiet. We also like the basket configuration even more than the previous Bosch. Cons: Reason for one reduced star is this: The plastic sliverwear basket towards the front "catches" on the plastic edge inside the dishwasher. At first we thought the bottom basket "clicked" in somehow but nope. It's actually slightly catching. I've uploaded two images to this review to better show the issue. I think would still buy this again but do think this warrants one reduction in stars and hope that I don't eventually rip or tear something. I hope the engineers at Bosch see this review and come up with a solution. Probably making that basket clip just a little shorter so it can't catch?
